title: Git
label: Git
desc: Distributed version control: snapshots, branches and history you can rewrite.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install Git, check the version and set the identity used by every commit.

snippets.code:
# Check what is already installed
git --version

# Debian and Ubuntu
sudo apt install git

# Fedora and RHEL
sudo dnf install git

# Arch
sudo pacman -S git

# Alpine
sudo apk add git

# macOS
brew install git

# Windows
winget install --id Git.Git -e

# Name and email are recorded in every commit, so set them first
git config --global user.name "Felipe Souza"
git config --global user.email "felipe@example.com"

# New repositories start on main instead of master
git config --global init.defaultBranch main

# Offline manual for any command
git help rebase
git help -g

sections.title: Configuration
sections.description: Read and write settings in the system, global and local scopes.

snippets.code:
# Every value with the file it came from
git config --list --show-origin

# Read one value
git config user.email

# Write to system, global and repository scope
git config --system core.pager "less -FRX"
git config --global core.editor "nvim"
git config --local pull.rebase true

# Short names for the commands typed all day
git config --global alias.st "status -sb"
git config --global alias.lg "log --oneline --graph --decorate --all"
git config --global alias.unstage "restore --staged"
git config --global alias.last "show --stat HEAD"

# Then: git st, git lg, git unstage notes.md, git last

# Edit the global config file directly
git config --global --edit

# Windows checkouts keep CRLF, the repository keeps LF
git config --global core.autocrlf true

# Ignore patterns shared by every repository on this machine
git config --global core.excludesFile ~/.config/git/ignore

# Cache credentials for an hour
git config --global credential.helper "cache --timeout=3600"

sections.title: Init and Clone
sections.description: Create a repository or copy an existing one over HTTPS or SSH.

snippets.code:
# Repository in the current folder, with the initial branch named
git init -b main

# Folder and repository in one call
git init cheatrs

# Bare repository to serve over SSH
git init --bare /srv/git/cheatrs.git

# Full clone over HTTPS
git clone https://github.com/cheatrs/cheatrs.git

# SSH clone into a specific folder
git clone git@github.com:cheatrs/cheatrs.git cheatrs-work

# Last commit only, enough for CI and build images
git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/cheatrs/cheatrs.git

# Bring submodules along
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/cheatrs/cheatrs.git

# Clone from a local folder, sharing objects instead of copying them
git clone --local ~/Projects/cheatrs ~/backup/cheatrs

sections.title: Snapshots
sections.description: Inspect the working tree, the index and how branches differ.

snippets.code:
# Short status with branch and tracking info
git status -sb

# Unstaged changes
git diff

# Staged changes, exactly what the next commit would record
git diff --staged

# Ignore whitespace noise while reviewing
git diff -w

# Commits on feature/login that main does not have
git diff main...feature/login

# One commit with its full patch
git show 4f2a1c3

# The same file compared across two branches
git diff main:src/main.rs feature/login:src/main.rs

# Stable, script-friendly output
git status --porcelain=v1

# Summary of the last three commits instead of the patch
git diff --stat HEAD~3

# Stage everything, then review it before committing
git add -A
git diff --staged --stat

sections.title: Staging
sections.description: Choose what goes into the next commit, hunk by hunk if needed.

snippets.code:
# Stage one file and a whole folder
git add src/main.rs
git add tests/

# Stage every change in the repository, deletions included
git add -A

# Stage only some hunks of a file
git add -p src/data.rs

# Unstage a file but keep the edits in the working tree
git restore --staged src/main.rs

# Same effect with the older spelling
git reset HEAD src/main.rs

# Discard unstaged edits of one file
git restore src/main.rs

# Renames and deletions are recorded by the index
git mv old_name.rs new_name.rs
git rm docs/draft.md

# Stop tracking a file but keep it on disk
git rm --cached secrets.env

sections.title: Commits
sections.description: Record changes and fix the last commit before it is published.

snippets.code:
# Stage tracked edits and commit in one step
git commit -am "fix: handle empty config file"

# Multi-line message written in the editor
git commit

# Show the diff while writing the message
git commit -v

# Rewrite the message of the last local commit
git commit --amend -m "fix: handle missing config file"

# Add a forgotten file, keeping the message
git add src/config.rs
git commit --amend --no-edit

# Change the author of the last commit
git commit --amend --author="Felipe Souza <felipe@example.com>" --no-edit

# Empty commit, useful to trigger a pipeline
git commit --allow-empty -m "ci: rerun pipeline"

# Mark this change as a fixup for a later autosquash rebase
git commit --fixup 9c1e0b2

sections.title: History
sections.description: Browse commits by branch, path, message, content and date.

snippets.code:
# Compact graph of every branch
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all

# Last five commits by one author
git log --author="Felipe" -5 --oneline

# History of a single path, following renames
git log --follow --oneline src/data.rs

# Commits that added or removed the string retry_limit
git log -S "retry_limit" --oneline

# Commits whose message matches a pattern
git log --grep="fix:" --oneline

# Line-by-line authorship of a range
git blame -L 40,60 src/main.rs

# Commits inside a date window
git log --since="2026-01-01" --until="2026-06-30" --oneline

# Who changed how much, ignoring merge commits
git shortlog -sn --no-merges

sections.title: Branching
sections.description: Create, list, rename and delete branches.

snippets.code:
# Local branches with upstream and last commit
git branch -vv

# Create and switch in one step
git switch -c feature/login

# Jump back to the previous branch
git switch -

# Delete a branch already merged
git branch -d feature/login

# Delete a branch that was never merged
git branch -D experiment/spike

# Rename the current branch
git branch -m feature/login feature/auth

# Branches already contained in main
git branch --merged main

# Branches with commits main does not have
git branch --no-merged main

# Remote-tracking branches
git branch -r

sections.title: Merging
sections.description: Bring another branch in, with or without a merge commit.

snippets.code:
# Merge feature/login into the current branch
git switch main
git merge feature/login

# Always keep a merge commit, even when fast-forward is possible
git merge --no-ff feature/login -m "merge: feature/login"

# Refuse to merge unless it is a fast-forward
git merge --ff-only origin/main

# Preview what the merge would bring
git log --oneline HEAD..feature/login

# Combine the branch into a single staged change
git merge --squash feature/login
git commit -m "feat: add login screen"

# Stop a merge in progress
git merge --abort

# Finish a merge after resolving the conflicts
git add src/auth.rs
git commit

# Or let Git continue with the prepared message
git merge --continue

sections.title: Rebasing
sections.description: Replay commits on a new base and reshape local history.

snippets.code:
# Replay the current branch on top of main
git switch feature/login
git rebase main

# Squash and reorder the last four commits
git rebase -i HEAD~4

# Fold fixup commits into their targets
git rebase -i --autosquash main

# Move only the commits after 3f9c2a1 onto main
git rebase --onto main 3f9c2a1 feature/login

# Update branches that point at rebased commits (Git 2.38+)
git rebase --update-refs main

# Give up and return to the state before the rebase
git rebase --abort

# Linear pulls instead of merge commits
git config --global pull.rebase true
git pull --rebase origin main

# Skip one commit and keep going
git rebase --skip

# Amend the conflict resolution of the current step
git add src/auth.rs
git rebase --continue

sections.title: Remotes
sections.description: Manage the repositories this clone talks to.

snippets.code:
# Remotes with their URLs
git remote -v

# Add, rename, change URL and remove
git remote add origin git@github.com:cheatrs/cheatrs.git
git remote rename origin upstream
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/cheatrs/cheatrs.git
git remote remove backup

# Publish a branch and set its upstream
git push -u origin feature/login

# Later pushes only need the remote and the branch
git push origin feature/login

# Delete a branch on the remote
git push origin --delete feature/login

# Fetch every remote and drop branches deleted upstream
git fetch --all --prune

# Start tracking a remote branch that already exists
git switch -c feature/docs origin/feature/docs

# See what a fetch would bring, without changing anything
git fetch --dry-run origin

sections.title: Tags
sections.description: Mark releases with lightweight or annotated tags.

snippets.code:
# Lightweight tag on the current commit
git tag v1.0.0

# Annotated tag with message, author and date
git tag -a v1.4.0 -m "release 1.4.0"

# Tag an older commit
git tag -a v1.3.0 8b7d2f1 -m "release 1.3.0"

# Tags matching a pattern
git tag -l "v1.*"

# Tag data and the commit it points to
git show v1.4.0

# Push one tag, or all of them
git push origin v1.4.0
git push origin --tags

# Delete locally, then on the remote
git tag -d v1.3.0
git push origin --delete v1.3.0

# Inspect the code at a release (detached HEAD)
git switch --detach v1.4.0

sections.title: Stashing
sections.description: Park unfinished work and come back to it later.

snippets.code:
# Save the working tree with a label
git stash push -m "wip: login validation"

# Include untracked files
git stash push -u -m "wip: new endpoint"

# Keep the changes in place and stash a copy
git stash push -k -m "wip: keep both"

# Stack of saved states
git stash list

# Patch of the newest entry
git stash show -p stash@{0}

# Apply the newest entry and remove it
git stash pop

sections.title: Undoing Things
sections.description: Take back commits and edits, locally or after they were published.

snippets.code:
# Unstage everything, files stay edited
git reset

# Move the branch back one commit, changes stay staged
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Move back one commit and discard the changes
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Undo a published commit with a new commit
git revert 4f2a1c3
git revert --no-edit HEAD

# Revert a merge commit against its first parent
git revert -m 1 9b3c7d1

# Every position HEAD has had, the way back after a bad reset
git reflog
git reset --hard HEAD@{2}

# Restore a file from an older commit
git restore --source=HEAD~1 src/deleted.rs

sections.title: Conflicts
sections.description: Find conflicted files, pick a side and close the operation.

snippets.code:
# Files left unresolved
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U

# Short status marks them with U
git status --short

# See the markers inside one file
git diff src/auth.rs

# Keep this branch's version or the incoming one
git restore --ours src/auth.rs
git restore --theirs src/auth.rs

# During a rebase the sides are swapped:
# --ours is main, --theirs is the commit being replayed

# Resolve file by file with the configured tool
git mergetool src/auth.rs

# Mark resolved and finish the operation
git add src/auth.rs
git merge --continue   # or: git rebase --continue

# Reuse previous resolutions of the same conflict
git config --global rerere.enabled true

sections.title: Cherry-pick
sections.description: Copy individual commits onto the current branch.

snippets.code:
# Apply one commit from another branch
git cherry-pick 4f2a1c3

# Record the source hash in the new message
git cherry-pick -x 4f2a1c3

# Apply without committing, to edit first
git cherry-pick -n 4f2a1c3

# Commits after 8b7d2f1 up to 4f2a1c3
git cherry-pick 8b7d2f1..4f2a1c3

# Change of a merge commit relative to its first parent
git cherry-pick -m 1 9b3c7d1

# Give up when a pick hits conflicts
git cherry-pick --abort

sections.title: Bisect
sections.description: Binary search the history to find the commit that broke something.

snippets.code:
# Start a session and mark the ends
git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good v1.3.0

# Let the test decide: exit 0 is good, 1 is bad, 125 is skipped
git bisect run cargo test --quiet --test regression

# Print the session log
git bisect log

# Finish and return to the original branch
git bisect reset

sections.title: Worktrees
sections.description: Check out several branches at once from a single repository.

snippets.code:
# Second checkout of the same repository, on another branch
git worktree add ../cheatrs-hotfix hotfix/login

# New branch in a new folder
git worktree add -b feature/docs ../cheatrs-docs main

# Detached worktree to inspect a release
git worktree add --detach ../cheatrs-v1 v1.4.0

# Worktrees and the branch each one holds
git worktree list

# Remove one, then clean administrative leftovers
git worktree remove ../cheatrs-hotfix
git worktree prune

sections.title: Ignoring Files
sections.description: Keep build output, secrets and editor noise out of the index.

snippets.code:
# Build output
target/
dist/

# Environment files, but keep the example
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

# Editor and OS noise
.idea/
.vscode/
.DS_Store

# Ignore logs while keeping the folder
logs/*
!logs/.gitkeep

# Which rule is hiding this path
git check-ignore -v target/debug/build

# Ignore a file only on this machine
echo "notes.local.md" >> .git/info/exclude

# Same patterns in every repository
git config --global core.excludesFile ~/.config/git/ignore

# A committed file stays tracked even after being ignored
git rm --cached config/production.yml
git commit -m "chore: stop tracking production config"

# Preview what would be removed from the index
git rm --cached -n config/production.yml

sections.title: Hooks
sections.description: Run scripts automatically before commits and pushes.

snippets.code:
# Hooks only run when they are executable
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/commit-msg

# Share hooks through the repository instead of .git/hooks
git config core.hooksPath .githooks

# Skip hooks for a single command
git commit --no-verify -m "wip: skip hooks"

sections.title: Common Recipes
sections.description: Small sequences for the situations that come up most.

snippets.code:
# Undo the last commit but keep the work staged
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Fix the message of the last local commit
git commit --amend

# Match the remote exactly, discarding local commits and edits
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/main

# Delete local branches already merged into main
git branch --merged main | grep -v -E '^\*|main' | xargs -r git branch -d

# Remove untracked files, preview first
git clean -nd
git clean -fd

# Keep a fork in sync with the original project
git remote add upstream https://github.com/original/project.git
git fetch upstream
git switch main
git merge --ff-only upstream/main
git push origin main
